episode_title: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

real_qa.q: How did Jackie Liberto grow her real estate brokerage to 119 agents in 19 months while retaining all but seven agents?
real_qa.r: Jackie Liberto retained 112 of 119 agents by focusing on authentic engagement and holistic care—supporting agents' personal health, family health, and business health. Of the seven who left, two exited real estate entirely and two left for personal reasons unrelated to the brokerage. She emphasizes caring about individuals as people first rather than prioritizing production numbers, using a mentoring program that compresses the first six months into 60 days and implementing systematic onboarding via Asana with regular four-to-six-week new agent orientations.

real_qa.q: What is the Emerald Coast Agent Panel and how has it impacted agent recruitment and community engagement?
real_qa.r: The Emerald Coast Agent Panel is a quarterly open-forum event that began in December 2020 after Jackie Liberto's top producers reported increased networking interest. Held at a local church venue with capacity for over 100 people, it features panels of top producers, lenders, and title company professionals—including external speakers like Brent Scott—and is open to all industry professionals, buyers, and sellers. Starting in 2022, it expanded to include breakout panels and half-day training sessions every other month, with no company recruitment messaging, focusing purely on community value and industry collaboration.
real_qa.requete: Emerald Coast Agent Panel real estate

real_qa.q: What onboarding and mentoring system does Jackie Liberto use to prevent new agents from falling through the cracks?
real_qa.r: Jackie Liberto uses Asana for systematic onboarding with every staff member assigned a role in the process. New agents undergo a four-to-six-week orientation returning to day-one checklist items to ensure no steps are missed. Mentorship is handled by two people—Jackie herself and an agent named Tanya—who conduct weekly two-hour Monday meetings, provide phone and FaceTime support, record all sessions for those unable to attend, and cycle through four training platforms on repeat with continuous feedback refinement.
real_qa.requete: Asana onboarding new real estate agents system

real_qa.q: How does Jackie Liberto's interview process for recruiting agents differ from traditional brokerage recruiting?
real_qa.r: Rather than providing answers or directing conversation, Jackie begins interviews by asking 'Why are you here?' or 'Why now?'—seeking to understand each agent's specific pain points and motivations before tailoring her pitch. This approach reveals whether an agent is frustrated with other brokerages, seeking creative freedom, or responding to other drivers, allowing Jackie to address actual needs instead of assumptions. She emphasizes that agents want to be heard, and this initial listening sets the tone for a person-focused rather than production-focused relationship.
real_qa.requete: recruiting interview questions real estate agents

real_qa.q: What personal follow-up system does Jackie Liberto implement to support agents after they join her brokerage?
real_qa.r: Jackie sets calendar reminders and recurring events for each new agent to ensure she follows up every three days, monitoring their wellbeing and life circumstances. She connects with agents on Facebook to stay aware of challenges they share publicly, then reaches out proactively—for example, texting 'I know you had a tough week last week, are you feeling better?'—demonstrating authentic care that cannot be faked and that agents recognize immediately.

real_qa.q: What is Jackie Liberto's core philosophy on agent production versus agent wellbeing?
real_qa.r: Jackie prioritizes agent wellness and personal happiness over production targets. She tells agents 'run your own race'—whether they want to close one transaction per month or ten—and commits to supporting any production level as long as agents are 'whole and happy and healthy.' She explicitly states in initial conversations that she cares more about them as individuals than their production numbers, a principle she calls 'retraining brains' to reset expectations from competitive brokerage cultures.

guest.bio_context: Jackie Liberto is a Florida native and military family member who obtained her real estate license in 2016 and worked as an agent for three and a half years before obtaining her broker's license. She opened her brokerage in March 2020 during the global pandemic and has grown it to 119 agents across three companies in 19 months, with a staff of six people.
